prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: which are the 3 best-selling products of each category by 2025 net revenue? Use the sales rows whose order_date falls in 2025. Keep exactly 3 products per category, or all of them when a category has fewer than 3 with sales; when products tie on revenue, the lower product_id comes first. Return three columns, in this order: category_name, product_id and revenue, the product's 2025 net revenue. Return one row for each product kept. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check which ranking function the filter reads: the question wants exactly 3 products per category.
A function that gives tied rows the same number can keep a fourth product; one that numbers every row apart needs the stated tie-break as its last sort key.
starter_sql:
WITH product_rev AS (  -- one row per product with 2025 sales
  SELECT category_name, product_id, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS revenue
  FROM sales
  WHERE order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY category_name, product_id
),
ranked AS (  -- one row per product with 2025 sales
  SELECT category_name, product_id, revenue,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_name ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rn
  FROM product_rev
)
SELECT category_name, product_id, revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 3
why_this_works: ROW_NUMBER with product_id after the revenue numbers tied products apart, so rn <= 3 keeps exactly 3 per category.
